Why move from scattered terminals to Nomi

Area Scattered terminals Nomi workbench
Parallel visibility Dozens of terminal tabs; hard to spot which agent is waiting or stuck Unified Agent Board with live status, CPU/RAM and approval priority
Model configuration Editing env vars and dotfiles per CLI; configs overwrite each other Connect once in Nomi; 4-protocol gateway scopes only to Nomi child processes
Reviewing edits Scrolling past terminal logs and running git diff manually Built-in changed-file cards, side workspace diff review and one-click undo
Credential safety Full home-directory access exposes ~/.ssh, cloud tokens and .env macOS system sandbox + prompt-injection taint guard on external reads
Footprint Multiple Electron IDEs consuming gigabytes of RAM ~25 MB Go + Wails core with automatic memory-pressure pause
Desktop character · Optional

The desktop character is optional. Turn it off if you don't need it.

The workbench works completely without it. When turned on, it sits in a corner of your desktop with expressions and task-progress bubbles. Off by default on fresh installs.

FAQ

Common questions before you install

Do I need a third-party API key to use Nomi?

No. If you already have Claude Code, Codex or other supported CLIs installed and signed in on your machine, you can pick them directly per conversation in Nomi — or run open-source local models via llama.cpp or Ollama.

Will connecting a third-party provider in Nomi overwrite my terminal CLI config?

No. Nomi's local gateway injects scoped environment variables only into child processes launched by Nomi. Your global ~/.claude, ~/.codex and official CLI sign-in states stay untouched.

Which agents and model protocols are supported?

Nomi includes built-in support for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Grok, dsh, Kimi Code and MiniMax Code plus custom ACP agents. Its local gateway translates between Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Responses, OpenAI Chat Completions and Gemini generateContent.

Are my chats, memories or codebase uploaded to Nomi servers?

No. Nomi has no cloud account system. Conversations, memories and knowledge-base indexes stay on your computer by default, API keys are encrypted in the OS keychain, and outbound masking strips keys before requests reach your chosen provider.

Do I have to keep the desktop character enabled?

No. It is completely optional and turned off by default on fresh installs. Every feature — Agent Board, side workspace, unified gateway and knowledge base — works identically with it off.

Is Nomi free and open source? Which platforms are supported?

Yes. Nomi is open source under the MIT license and free to use on Windows 10/11 (64-bit), macOS 12+ (Apple silicon & Intel) and Linux x86_64 (AppImage & .deb), with installers around 22–29 MB.
